assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: gap:resume

## Reasoning

### agent — yes

Hermes Agent 0.19.0 declares `-r/--resume <session_id>` on both the top-level parser and the `chat` subparser (`hermes_cli/_parser.py:157` and `:334`; the usage banner at `:48` reads `hermes --resume <session_id>  Resume a specific session by ID`), plus `-c/--continue` which `cmd_chat` resolves into `--resume` with the most recent session for the matching source (`hermes_cli/main.py:2450-2472`, `_resolve_last_session(source='cli')`).

Crucially for this scenario, resume REUSES the existing session row rather than forking a new one. `_preload_resumed_session` (`hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py:464-548`) loads the target's history, keeps `self.session_id` AS the target id, and then explicitly clears the terminal columns — `UPDATE sessions SET ended_at = NULL, end_reason = NULL WHERE id = ?` (the same statement `hermes_state.SessionDB.reopen_session` runs, `hermes_state.py:4334-4341`). New messages therefore land under the SAME `messages.session_id`, and the session upsert is `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE` (`hermes_state.py:3729-3747`) whose SET list does NOT include `started_at` — so the row's identity and birth timestamp survive the relaunch untouched. This is the store-level equivalent of claudecode appending to the same UUID transcript.

### daemon — full

Hermes writes no transcript files; the single shared SQLite store IS the transport (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/adapter.go` package doc, `agent.go` `Source: agent.ProcessOwnedStore`). Every signal this scenario asserts is keyed on `sessions.id`, which resume preserves:

- **"Same session_id reappears (not a new session row)"** — `Watcher.scanSessions` selects by `sessions.id` and `reconcile` keeps a per-id cursor (`watcher.go:278-419`). A resumed session is the same row, so `!emitted` is false and NO second `new_session` is emitted; the daemon keeps one session row across both PID lifetimes.
- **`ready → working` on the first new turn** — the second lifetime's user message grows `message_count`, so `grew` is true and `reconcile` emits an `EventActivity` with `Terminal` computed from `turnIsDone` (`watcher.go:408-419`, `:426-436`). `finish_reason='stop'` on the newest assistant row is Hermes' explicit turn boundary, so the arc settles back to ready without an idle heuristic.
- **"correctly attributed to the current PID lifetime"** — `DiscoverPID` matches on cwd + the full command line (`pid.go`), and the daemon's same-PID cleanup (`core/application/services/pid_manager.go:540`, issue #169) retires the second lifetime's `proc-<PID2>` presession once the store session re-binds to the new PID.

This is the same shape opencode's cell (the other `ProcessOwnedStore` column) already records green: `proc-<PID>` presession → handoff to the store id → turn cycle → `process_exited` → activity on the SAME store id after the exit.

### driver — gap:resume

`replaydata/agents/hermes/driver-interactive.sh` is the scaffold: its `resume` arm is `not_implemented`, and `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"`, so recipe-lint flags this recipe as a semantic_gap before recording. The port is mechanical — copy `step_resume` from `replaydata/agents/codex/driver-interactive.sh:410-443`, which already does the whole primitive in one step (Ctrl-D the REPL, wait for the tmux session to die, kill it, relaunch under a rotated tmux name). Only two hermes-specific substitutions are needed: relaunch `hermes chat -r "$resume_uuid" --no-restore-cwd` instead of `codex resume <uuid>`, and — the load-bearing part — do NOT re-run `resolve_session_id` afterwards. `resolve_session_id` binds to `started_at > SES_LAUNCH_TS[$ACTIVE]`, and resume leaves `started_at` at the ORIGINAL launch, so a re-resolution after the relaunch would find nothing (or worse, an unrelated newer row). Keep `SES_UUID`/`SES_TRANSCRIPT`/`EXPECTED_TURNS_SEEN` for the slot unchanged, exactly as codex's step_resume keeps its rollout. This is tooling work, not an observability limit — the cell records the moment the step lands.
caveats: PROVISIONAL on emission: daemon=full is derived from reading watcher.go/metrics.go plus the Hermes source that proves the row is reused, NOT from a live recording. What a doc read cannot settle is the exact scan-to-event timing of the reopen — the watcher emits nothing when `ended_at` flips back to NULL (`reconcile` returns early when neither `grew` nor `justEnded`), so the FIRST observable of the second lifetime is the activity event from the resumed turn's user message, not a separate 'session came back' event. The spec is written that way (v2_resume_rebind asserts kind=transcript_activity, not a state re-birth); record must confirm it.

The watcher's discovery filter is `started_at > now - maxAge` (watcher.go:285-288) and resume does NOT refresh `started_at` (the sessions upsert's ON CONFLICT SET list omits it, hermes_state.py:3737-3747). Resuming a session older than the daemon's maxAge window would therefore never be rediscovered. Out of scope for this scenario (the recipe resumes seconds later), but it is a real limit for a user resuming yesterday's session.

`sessions.cwd` is populated only for TUI sessions, so a `hermes chat` (source='cli') session borrows the cwd of the single live hermes process (`watcher.go:115-124`, `metrics.go:119-122`). `defaultLiveCWD` deliberately returns "" when MORE than one hermes session process is alive, so a recording with a second concurrent hermes session would leave this session unbound (no cwd → no PID discovery → no process_exited phase). Recording prerequisite, not a daemon defect.

`_preload_resumed_session` calls `resolve_resume_session_id` first: if the target is the empty head of a compression chain, Hermes resumes the DESCENDANT id instead and prints 'was compressed into <id>' (cli_agent_setup_mixin.py:490-503). That path would legitimately surface a different session_id. It cannot fire in this recipe (one short turn, no compaction), but a compaction-adjacent resume is a different cell.

`observations.cost_nonzero` is deliberately NOT asserted. Hermes reports `estimated_cost_usd = 0.0` under `billing_mode='subscription_included'`, and the adapter re-prices from irrlicht's own alias table instead (metrics.go:155-163) — so cost is nonzero only if the recording home's configured model is in `core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go`. record should promote it once the live model is known.

`observations.model` is left unpinned per the anti-pattern rule: the model comes from the recording home's `<HERMES_HOME>/config.yaml` (`model.default`), which is not knowable from here. record fills it from the recording.

sources.note: Lines 48, 157, 334 — `-r/--resume <session_id>` declared on both the top-level and `chat` parsers; usage banner documents 'Resume a specific session by ID'. Hermes Agent 0.19.0 (pyproject.toml:5).

_preload_resumed_session (464-548): keeps self.session_id AS the resumed id, replays its history, then `UPDATE sessions SET ended_at=NULL, end_reason=NULL WHERE id=?`. This is the proof that resume reuses the SAME row rather than minting a new one.

reopen_session (4334-4341) is the same UPDATE; the sessions upsert (3729-3747) is ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE with started_at absent from the SET list — id and birth timestamp are stable across the relaunch.
cmd_chat (2444-2500): resolves -c/--continue into --resume (by name or most-recent for source='cli'), then resolves --resume by title or direct id.

scanSessions/reconcile (278-419) key every cursor on sessions.id, so a reopened row emits no second new_session; turnIsDone (426-436) reads finish_reason='stop' as the explicit turn boundary that settles the resumed turn back to ready.
Source is agent.ProcessOwnedStore over $HERMES_HOME/state.db — no transcript files exist, so session identity is the store row, which is exactly what resume preserves.
Line 540 — HandlePIDAssigned cleans up sessions sharing the same PID (issue #169); this is what retires the second lifetime's proc-<PID2> presession once the store session re-binds.
The `resume` arm is not_implemented and DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn" — the concrete anchor for driver=gap:resume.
step_resume (410-443) is the reference port: Ctrl-D, wait for tmux death, rotate the tmux name, relaunch resuming the SAME id, and deliberately do NOT re-resolve the transcript/uuid.
The sibling ProcessOwnedStore cell, already green — presession → handoff → turn cycle → process_exited → activity on the SAME store id after the exit. This cell's spec follows its shape.

preconditions: hermes >= 0.19.0 on PATH and an inference provider configured in <HERMES_HOME>/config.yaml with credentials
HERMES_HOME exported to the recording home so the run writes to an isolated state.db
sqlite3 on PATH (the driver reads session id and turn completion straight out of state.db)
NO other hermes session process alive during the recording — defaultLiveCWD returns "" when more than one is running, and a source='cli' session has no stored cwd to fall back on
drive-hermes-interactive.sh must expose the `resume` step type (currently not_implemented; port step_resume from drive-codex-interactive.sh:410-443)
setup: One cwd under <staging>/cwd/, reused across both lifetimes. Hermes only cd's into a session's recorded cwd on resume when `sessions.cwd` is non-empty, which it never is for source='cli' — pass --no-restore-cwd anyway so the behaviour is pinned rather than incidental.

The `resume` step must do the whole primitive: Ctrl-D the REPL (graceful exit → the process_exited the spec asserts), kill the tmux session, then relaunch `hermes chat -r "$resume_uuid" --no-restore-cwd` in the SAME cwd under a rotated tmux session name. Reuse the ACTIVE slot — do not alloc_slot; this is one session with two PID lifetimes.

Do NOT call resolve_session_id after the relaunch. It binds to `started_at > SES_LAUNCH_TS[$ACTIVE]`, and resume leaves started_at at the ORIGINAL launch (the sessions upsert never updates it), so re-resolution would miss the row or bind a foreign one. Keep SES_UUID/SES_TRANSCRIPT/EXPECTED_TURNS_SEEN for the slot unchanged across the resume — EXPECTED_TURNS_SEEN in particular, so the post-resume wait_turn blocks for the SECOND finish_reason='stop' rather than returning on the first.
The session id must be captured BEFORE the resume: resolve_session_id already runs inside wait_turn, so the turn-1 wait_turn is what binds it.

Reply with exactly the word: again

verify: events.jsonl shows a proc-<PID> presession in ready, then the store session id born in ready (a DIFFERENT session_id) once Hermes INSERTs the sessions row on the first user message
ready → working → ready for turn 1 on the store session id
a process_exited event on the store session id after turn 1 (the Ctrl-D performed by the resume step)
the SAME store session id shows transcript_activity AFTER that process_exited — NOT a new session id. This is the spec's 'Same session_id reappears (not a new session row)'
ready → working → ready for turn 2 on the SAME store session id — each lifetime's arc is independently correct
exactly ONE hermes session row exists in the dashboard across both lifetimes; the second lifetime's proc-<PID2> presession is retired by the same-PID cleanup
final session state is ready; no tool calls in either turn
state.db: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE session_id='<id>' AND role='user'` is 2 — both turns landed under one session_id
recipe.scope_note: Records the clean-exit-then-resume variant only, matching claudecode's and codex's cells for this scenario. The spec's second variant (repeated kill+resume across many PID lifetimes) shares the same observability surface and can be a follow-up cell. Hermes' resume is explicit (`hermes chat -r <id>`), and unlike claudecode/codex there is no transcript file to reopen — continuity is the SQLite sessions row, whose ended_at/end_reason are cleared on resume.
